# Tokyo Family Trip Plan: 18–24 Mar 2026

A kid-friendly week in Tokyo with a mix of sightseeing, anime/manga, culture, and budget-conscious food. Plan assumes 4 people, using a balance of trains, walking, and a few paid attractions to keep the trip under **JPY 180,000** excluding flights.

## 7-Day Itinerary and Budget by Day

| Day | Focus | Main Stops | Approx. Daily Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 18 | Central Tokyo arrival day | Asakusa, Senso-ji, Nakamise, Sumida area | **JPY 18,000** |
| Mar 19 | Anime + modern city | Akihabara, Ueno, Ameyoko | **JPY 24,000** |
| Mar 20 | Traditional Tokyo | Meiji Jingu, Harajuku, Shibuya | **JPY 20,000** |
| Mar 21 | Family icons + waterfront | Odaiba, teamLab-style indoor art, Tokyo Bay area | **JPY 32,000** |
| Mar 22 | Park + neighborhood day | Shinjuku Gyoen, Ikebukuro, Sunshine City | **JPY 22,000** |
| Mar 23 | Hands-on culture | Edo-Tokyo Museum area alternatives, Kappabashi, Ueno | **JPY 18,000** |
| Mar 24 | Easy departure day | last shopping, local breakfast, airport transfer | **JPY 16,000** |

## Day-by-Day Family Plan

### Day 1: Asakusa Welcome Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and take a gentle walk around **Senso-ji** and **Nakamise Street**.
- **Afternoon:** Ride the riverfront area near **Sumida Park** for skyline views and a relaxed first day.
- **Food:** Budget lunch at a soba shop or tempura set near Asakusa; look for family meals around **JPY 800–1,200 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** **Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center** and indoor shopping arcades nearby.
- **Transportation tip:** Use **Tokyo Metro + walking**; Asakusa is easy to navigate with kids and strollers.

### Day 2: Akihabara Anime Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Morning:** Explore **Akihabara** for anime, manga, capsule toys, and character stores.
- **Afternoon:** Move to **Ueno Park** for open space, then browse **Ameyoko** for snacks and casual shopping.
Media: Alt=Afternoon:** Move to **Ueno Park** for open space, then browse **Ameyoko** for snacks and casual shopping, Tokyo, Japan
- **Food:** Low-cost curry rice, ramen, or gyudon in Akihabara; budget **JPY 900–1,300 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Spend longer in **manga/anime shops** and arcades in Akihabara.
- **Transportation tip:** Use **JR Yamanote Line** between Ueno, Akihabara, and nearby stops to minimize transfers.

### Day 3: Culture and City Views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Meiji Jingu** for a traditional shrine experience and a quieter start.
- **Afternoon:** Walk **Harajuku** and then head to **Shibuya** for the crossing and city energy.
- **Food:** Cheap lunch at a standing noodle shop or rice bowl place in Harajuku/Shibuya side streets.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Indoor shopping in **Shibuya Parco** or **Laforet Harajuku**.
- **Transportation tip:** Combine **JR Yamanote** and short walks; avoid taxis in central Tokyo unless kids are exhausted.

### Day 4: Odaiba Family Fun
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Odaiba** for waterfront views, wide walkways, and family-friendly attractions.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one paid indoor experience such as a digital art museum-style venue or a science/interactive museum.
- **Food:** Food court lunch or conveyor-belt sushi; budget **JPY 1,000–1,500 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Odaiba works well in rain because many attractions are indoor.
- **Transportation tip:** Use the **Yurikamome** line for scenic transit; kids usually enjoy the elevated ride.

### Day 5: Park Time and Indoor Entertainment
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Relax in **Shinjuku Gyoen** if weather is good; it is ideal for a slower family day.
- **Afternoon:** Go to **Ikebukuro** and **Sunshine City** for shopping, aquarium-style entertainment, and kid-friendly indoor spaces.
- **Food:** Budget ramen or udon in Ikebukuro; plan **JPY 800–1,200 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Stay inside **Sunshine City** for shopping, viewing, and entertainment.
- **Transportation tip:** Pick one base neighborhood and keep walking distances short to avoid kid fatigue.

### Day 6: Traditional Hands-On Tokyo
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kappabashi** for kitchenware streets and fun browsing; great for souvenirs without high costs.
- **Afternoon:** Add a traditional craft or cultural activity such as a short workshop, temple visit, or old-town walking route in nearby areas.
- **Food:** Cheap lunch at a local set-meal restaurant or donburi shop; budget **JPY 900–1,300 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Indoor shopping in **Kappabashi** and nearby covered arcades.
- **Transportation tip:** Use **subway + short taxi only if needed**; this day is best kept compact and flexible.

### Day 7: Easy Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Morning:** Keep it light with breakfast near your hotel and a final souvenir stop.
- **Afternoon:** Transfer to the airport with enough buffer for family check-in and snacks.
- **Food:** Convenience-store breakfast or simple café meal; budget **JPY 500–1,000 per person**.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Indoor station shopping or hotel lounge time before departure.
- **Transportation tip:** Leave early for the airport and use the most direct rail option from your hotel area.

## Budget Plan for 4 People

| Category | Estimated Total |
|---|---|
| Local transportation | **JPY 24,000–32,000** |
| Admission / paid activities | **JPY 52,000–68,000** |
| Food and snacks | **JPY 56,000–70,000** |
| Souvenirs / small extras | **JPY 12,000–18,000** |
| Buffer for surprises | **JPY 8,000–12,000** |
| **Trip total** | **JPY 152,000–180,000** |

## Quick Travel Tips for Families

- Stay near **Ueno, Asakusa, or Shinjuku** for easy rail access and simpler daily routing.
- Use **IC cards** like Suica/PASMO for trains and convenience-store purchases.
- Plan one major activity per day plus one backup indoor option to reduce stress.
- For kids, build in snack breaks every 2–3 hours.
- Keep one day lighter than the rest so the trip feels fun instead of rushed.

## Sources

- Tokyo tourism overview: https://www.gotokyo.org/en/
- Tokyo Metro route planning: https://www.tokyometro.jp/en/
- JR East travel information: https://www.jreast.co.jp/e/
